title: fix(types,components): the zod mirrors stop authoring defaults
body:
Fixes #7735

Implements the director ruling on #7735 (decision batch #69, 2026-09-07; maintainer reply 「其他同意」), option 乙. **A validator validates; it does not write values into an author's document.** The renderer's fallback is the single authoritative default, the JSDoc `@default` describes it, and the zod mirror carries none.

## The defect

`.default(v)` on a mirror member is not documentation — `parse` SUBSTITUTES `v` into the output when the key is absent. One authored document therefore took two shapes depending on whether it had been through `safeValidateSchema`, and where the two faces disagreed the mirror silently won:

| key | mirror wrote | the renderer applies |
|---|---|---|
| `ContainerSchema.maxWidth` | `'lg'` | `container.tsx:26`  `?? 'xl'` |
| `FlexSchema.align` | `'center'` | `flex.tsx:18`  `\|\| 'start'` |

⚠️ Those are the two rows the ruling names, **not the population**. The contract
review asked for the rest and the answer is **six**: auditing all 22 layout keys
against their renderers adds `grid.columns` (mirror `3` / `grid.tsx`'s own
`let baseCols = 2`), `text.variant` (`'body'` / none — a bare node, objectui#6942),
`resizable.withHandle` (`true` / forwarded bare, so `undefined` draws NO grip) and
`page.template` (`'default'` / a null template falls through to the `pageType`
dispatch, and `'default'` is a real `TEMPLATE_REGISTRY` key, so the substitution
really did skip that dispatch). A consumer that renders `result.data` sees a
different result on all six.

Measured on the built face before the change, and again after:

```
before   safeValidateSchema({type:'container'}) -> {"type":"container","maxWidth":"lg","centered":true}
         safeValidateSchema({type:'flex'})      -> {"type":"flex","direction":"row","justify":"start","align":"center","gap":2,"wrap":false}
after    safeValidateSchema({type:'container'}) -> {"type":"container"}
         safeValidateSchema({type:'flex'})      -> {"type":"flex"}
         safeValidateSchema({type:'stack'})     -> {"type":"stack"}        (control: never authored defaults)
```

## The population — the ruling's arithmetic, re-derived

The ruling says "45 `.default()` sites across the seven `*.zod.ts` files". Re-derived on `origin/main` `fc32921` with the TypeScript AST rather than a text search: **41 real call sites in 5 files**. Four of the 45 text matches are prose inside docblocks, and the two files carrying them have nothing to remove.

| file | raw `.default(` text | in a comment | **call sites** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layout.zod.ts` | 22 | 0 | **22** |
| `crud.zod.ts` | 11 | 0 | **11** |
| `form.zod.ts` | 5 | 0 | **5** |
| `views.zod.ts` | 2 | 0 | **2** |
| `app.zod.ts` | 1 | 0 | **1** |
| `objectql.zod.ts` | 3 | **3** | **0** |
| `complex.zod.ts` | 1 | **1** | **0** |
| `base.zod.ts` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| | **45** | **4** | **41** |

This confirms the PM's count exactly. `objectql.zod.ts` and `complex.zod.ts` are untouched — editing them to reach "45" would have been inventing a diff.

## ⚠️ Breaking for consumers that read `result.data`

Stated plainly here as well as in the changeset: `validateSchema` /
`safeValidateSchema` no longer substitute, so for a document that omits one of
these 41 keys the key is now **absent** from the parsed output. Every one of the
41 changes output; six of them change rendering for a consumer that renders
`result.data` (the table above). Readers of a parsed default must apply their own
fallback. The accept set is untouched — nothing that parsed before is refused now.

## Accept set: unchanged, and that was checked rather than assumed

`.default()` can carry optionality as well as a value: a member written `.default(x)` with no `.optional()` is optional *because of* the default, and removing it naively makes the key **required** — a silent accept-set narrowing on a published surface, which this ruling did not authorise. All 41 were spelled `TYPE.optional().default(v).describe(…)`, so **0 of 41** were carrying optionality. Nothing that parsed before is refused now. This narrows `parse` OUTPUT only, which is the conformance limb of clause ②, not clause ② itself.

## Consumer census — execution note 1

The only risk of option 乙 is a consumer that reads a substituted default off `result.data`. Measured, not assumed. **Count: 0.**

Four modules import `@object-ui/types/zod` outside tests:

| consumer | what it reads | affected |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts` | `safeValidateSchema(content).success` only | no |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` | `result.data.{type,id,label,title,children}` — none ever carried a default | no |
| `packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx` | `ObjectMapConfigSchema.safeParse(config)` for `.success` / `.error`; returns the raw `config`, discarding `.data`. `ObjectMapConfigSchema` lives in `objectql.zod.ts`, which had **0** call sites | no |
| `scripts/measure-strict-authoring-face.mjs` | its `keyProbe` twin is rebuilt with `z.any().optional()` leaves, so defaults never reach it; `undeclaredKeys` walks `Object.keys(input)`, so extra keys in the parse output are invisible to it either way. Not wired into any gate or workflow | no |

⭐ **The render path never ran this validator at all** — the open question os-sam raised in [comment 5564118219](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7735#issuecomment-5564118219) ("whether any document parse goes through `ContainerSchema`'s zod mirror in practice"). `SchemaRenderer` calls `validateSchema` from **`@object-ui/core`**, a structural validator returning `{valid, errors}` with no zod, no `.data` and no substitution. The mirror's `.default()` only ever reached documents put through `@object-ui/types/zod` deliberately — the CLI and external consumers.

Empirically: **6 105 tests across `packages/types`, `packages/components`, `packages/cli`, `examples/schema-catalog` and `scripts/` pass unchanged**. Not one asserted a substituted default.

## Pin (i) — and the trap in the ruling's wording

⛔ Pin (i) is **not** a text search. Worded literally as the ruling puts it — *"no `.default(` under `packages/types/src/zod/**`"* — it is **red on the day it lands**, because the four docblock mentions are legitimate prose that survives the change, and the only way to make such a pin green would be to delete real prose. `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-authors-no-defaults-7735.test.ts` parses instead:

* every `X.default(…)` **CallExpression** under `packages/types/src/zod/**` — comments are not in the AST, so prose is invisible by construction;
* a walk of the whole schema graph reachable from the published barrel;
* the behavioural half (parse output carries no key the author did not write), with `stack` as the never-authored control;
* accept-set probes (every de-defaulted key still omissible).

It also carries the positive controls that keep a null result meaningful: the AST walker is shown finding `.describe()` on the very chains `.default()` used to sit in, and the discrimination itself is asserted — some mirror file still *mentions* `.default(` in prose, every such file has **0** call sites, and the text count exceeds the call count. That gap **is** the control.

`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/__tests__/registration-defaults-match-renderer-8229.test.ts` is pin (ii): it re-derives every `defaultProps`/fallback pair in `flex.tsx` and `stack.tsx` off disk and fails if any diverges.

### Both pins were ablated — they discriminate

Run from the committed tree, each leg proving the mutation reached disk before the run and that the restore was verified by blob hash, not by an exit code:

```
LEG A  reintroduce one .default() in layout.zod.ts
       mutation on disk: yes; blob differs from HEAD: YES
       × no mirror file contains a `.default()` CALL SITE
       × the residue that survives is entirely spec-derived, and it is not zero
       × every surviving `.default(` match is prose, and the AST census ignores all of them
       × container            (parse output regained "centered")
       Tests  4 failed | 19 passed (23)
       restored: diff=[] blob-match=YES

LEG B  put defaultProps.align back to 'center'
       align: 'center' occurrences = 1, align: 'start' = 0
       Tests  3 failed | 5 passed (8)
       restored: diff=[] blob-match=YES

LEG C  what a bare TEXT pin would have reported on this tree:
       packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts:1
       packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:3
       ⇒ red on landing, over four pieces of legitimate prose.
```

## What this does NOT reach — measured, and it is a real residue

Removing all 41 does **not** make `safeValidateSchema` stop substituting. **57 `ZodDefault` nodes remain reachable** from the published barrel afterwards, and — by the same call-site census that proves the mirror authors none — every one of them is inside a subschema imported by reference from `@objectstack/spec`:

```
{"type":"object-view","objectName":"account","navigation":{}}
  -> navigation: {"mode":"page","preventNavigation":false,"openNewTab":false,"size":"auto"}
{"type":"app","name":"a","title":"A"}          -> gains active:true, isDefault:false
{"type":"list-view",…,"sharing":{}}            -> sharing: {"type":"collaborative"}
{"type":"kanban",…,grouping.fields:[{field}]}  -> gains order:"asc", collapsed:false
```

So the "one authored document, two shapes" defect survives on those keys. Those values are written in `@objectstack/spec` and cannot be removed from this repository — restating them locally to strip them would be the "narrower than the contract it implements" shape `complex.zod.ts` already records twice. The pin documents the boundary and asserts the residue is non-zero as a **floor, not a ratchet** (the exact figure moves with every spec bump); what it does hold constant is the *attribution*. Recorded on #7735 for triage; ⛔ not filed as a card from here.

## #8229 — fully covered, and its census reproduces

⭐ **#8229 is fully covered by this PR.** Nothing of it narrows into a follow-up, so its author can mark it done once this lands. Its `defaultProps.align` face is reconciled (`'center'` → `'start'`, the value `flex.tsx:18` actually applies) and pin (ii) is a standing gate over exactly the surface it measured, so nothing of it narrows into a follow-up.

Its bounded census reproduces exactly: re-deriving it mechanically over `flex.tsx` + `stack.tsx` gives **8 comparable pairs, 1 disagreement** — `flex.align` — matching its table row for row.

## Out of scope — noted, not filed

Re-deriving that same comparison **repo-wide** found **55 comparable pairs and 7 disagreements**: the `flex.align` row fixed here, plus six more.

| file | key | `defaultProps` | renderer fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| `renderers/action/action-bar.tsx` | `variant` | `'outline'` | `'ghost'` |
| `renderers/action/action-button.tsx` | `size` | `'md'` | `'default'` |
| `renderers/action/action-group.tsx` | `size` | `'sm'` | `'default'` |
| `renderers/basic/pagination.tsx` | `totalPages` | `10` | `1` |
| `renderers/form/file-upload.tsx` | `buttonText` | `'Choose files'` | `'DROP PAYLOAD OR CLICK TO UPLOAD'` |
| `plugin-markdown/src/index.tsx` | `content` | a sample document | `''` |

⛔ **Not touched, and deliberately not filed as defects.** They are not six more instances of this bug: `defaultProps` is a designer **seed** as much as a default claim — `pagination`'s `totalPages: 10` and `flex`'s own three-button `children` array are seeds, not statements about what a key means when omitted — and whether the two roles may legitimately diverge is exactly the question #4631 is holding, `pm:on-hold`. Widening pin (ii) repo-wide would have decided that question by gate rather than by ruling. Recorded here for whoever takes #4631.

## Ruling note 3(ii) — re-measured against the renderer, and four tags corrected

⭐ **The first version of this PR reported note 3(ii) as already satisfied. That was
measured against the wrong reference** and the contract review was right to fail it.
Each JSDoc `@default` was compared with the value the **mirror** used to write; the
ruling asks for the **renderer's fallback**, which is the entire point of option 乙 —
the renderer is now the authoritative face, so a tag agreeing with the mirror proves
only that the docs copied the mirror. All four tags corrected below had matched the
mirror exactly, which is precisely why a mirror-referenced check called the face clean.

Re-measured against the renderer, all 41 de-defaulted keys:

| verdict | n |
|---|---|
| tag agrees with what the renderer applies | 19 |
| tag misdescribed the renderer — **corrected here** | **4** |
| no tag, deliberately (#7361 / #7734: two divergent consumers) | 2 |
| no registered renderer reads the key — "equals the renderer fallback" has no referent | 16 |

The four corrections, each following #7361's own rule (a tag states what the renderer
applies; where it applies nothing, the honest form is the absence of a tag plus prose
naming the read site):

| member | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `GridSchema.columns` | `@default 3` | `@default 2` + prose naming `grid.tsx`'s `baseCols` |
| `TextSchema.variant` | `@default 'body'` | no tag + prose naming `text.tsx` and objectui#6942 |
| `ResizableSchema.withHandle` | `@default true` | no tag + prose naming the bare forward and the grip gate |
| `PageNodeSchema.template` | `@default 'default'` | no tag + prose naming `resolveTemplate` and the `pageType` fall-through |

19 of the agreeing rows were confirmed too, 13 by the `schema.x ?? 'lit'` sweep and 6
by hand where the renderer uses another shape — `container.centered` (`!== false`),
`card.hoverable` / `card.clickable` (`|| isClickable` / `|| !!props.onClick`),
`aspect-ratio.ratio` (`|| 16 / 9`), `separator.orientation` and `icon.size` (forwarded
bare, the primitive's own default is what the tag names).

### The pin, and the narrowing it does not reach

`packages/types/src/__tests__/layout-default-jsdoc-7361.test.ts` gains the four rows —
same file, same rule, one instrument. Both sides are read off disk, every extraction has
a positive control, and the file now covers **8** rows plus 2 negative controls.

It also gains a discrimination control that is not hypothetical: `TextSchema.variant`'s
new prose **quotes** the retired `@default 'body'`, so the text is in the file while the
member publishes no tag. The pin asserts both — the extractor sees the quoted mention
and still returns an empty tag list, and it still finds a real tag on a neighbouring
member. Without it, "the tag list is empty" could have been passing because the
extractor had quietly stopped matching anything.

⚠️ **Declared narrowing.** The pin is row-by-row, not a sweep, and **33 of the 41 keys
stay unpinned**. That is a measured decision: these renderers do not express defaults
uniformly, and a generic `schema.x || 'lit'` sweep is blind to every shape that matters —
it scores `grid.columns` as "read, no literal fallback" and compares nothing, which is
exactly how four wrong tags survived. A general instrument would have to model an
initialiser (`let baseCols = 2`), a `!== false` read, a bare forward whose default is the
absence of an affordance, and a registry lookup returning `null` — and it would have to
decide what "the renderer for this type" means when two files register `'text'` with
non-overlapping `variant` vocabularies (`renderers/basic/text.tsx` and
`renderers/basic/elements.tsx` both do). Filed as **#8318** with the full 16-key list and
both open questions; not decided here.

### Ablation — the four new rows discriminate

```
LEG D  GridSchema.columns' tag back to 3
       '@default 3' on disk: 1; blob differs from pre-ablation: YES
       × carries exactly one `@default`, and it is grid.tsx's own initialiser
       × no longer publishes `3`, the value only the mirror ever wrote
       Tests  2 failed | 30 passed (32)      restored: blob-match=YES

LEG E  re-add the retired `@default 'body'` to TextSchema.variant
       occurrences on disk 1 -> 2 (1 in prose + 1 injected)
       × publishes NO `@default` block tag
       × the prose mentions the retired tag, and the extractor is not fooled by it
       Tests  2 failed | 30 passed (32)      restored: blob-match=YES
```

## Verification (patch round, head `d28d27a`)

| gate | verdict |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/components run type-check` | exit 0 (both `Done`) — `tsconfig.test.json` is in the run, and it caught a real error in the pin during round 1, so the test files are demonstrably in the program |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/components run lint` | exit 0, 0 errors; per changed file `layout.ts` 0/0, the extended pin 0/0, `text.tsx` 0 errors / 1 pre-existing warning, `flex.tsx` the same |
| `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` | round 1: 4 421 files judged; 94 pre-existing errors across 78 files, **0 in any file this PR touches**, 0 new warnings |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/ packages/cli/ examples/schema-catalog/ scripts/` | exit 0 — **8 491** passed, 0 failed |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/` | exit 0 — **2 204** passed, 0 failed |
| `check:comment-mask-corpus` · `check:unused-deps` | exit 0 — both re-run after the docblock rewrites |
| `check:sdui-registration-pins` | exit 0 measured at `a6ac2bb`; ⚠️ **declared**, not re-measured at `d28d27a`. Every line `packages/components` changed since is a comment (`git diff a6ac2bb -- packages/components` has no non-comment `+`/`-` line), so the bundle's registration set cannot have moved. Falsifiable: a red run of this gate on this branch reopens it. CI re-measures |
| `check:comment-mask-corpus` | exit 0 — the new gate from #8277, re-run on the merged head; no residue added |
| `check:control-bytes` · `check:doc-types` · `check:doc-snippets` · `check:doc-fences` · `check:spec-symbols` · `check:phantom-deps` · `check:handler-key-reads` · `check:unreferenced-sources` · `check:published-tsconfig-exclude` · `check:readme-exports` · `check:entry-guard` · `check:dist-completeness` · changeset-presence · changeset-no-major | exit 0 |

Every exit code was captured to disk before any output was read. `origin/main` merged at `3c6394c`; the suite above was re-run on the merged head `a6ac2bb`.

`needs:contract-review` is attached per the ruling's note 4 — the conformance limb (output shape narrows, accept set untouched), **not** clause ②.
